question: There has been a near miss incident where an experienced operator failed to respond to Level Alarm High (LAH) on the fuel tank, resulting in a LOC from the tank. Which of the following is the best way to learn lessons from all incidents and prevent reoccurrence?
options: Discuss the incident with the operator to ensure his understanding for the incident significance and they must respond appropriately to alarm in future
Investigate the incident and its root causes and ensure this is communicated to the wide audience
Accept that on this occasion a mistake was made. Offer the operator refresher training to manage alarms effectively
Suggest the organization to retrain the operator for a new role
correctOptionText: Investigate the incident and its root causes and ensure this is communicated to the wide audience
source: NEBOSH PSM Mock Exam Book extraction workbook

question: Under What circumstances does brittle fracture occur?
options: Form exposing materials to rapid and extreme temperature changes with uneven expansion and stress overcoming materials strength.
As a result of a repeated application of loads that, individually, do not create sufficient stress to cause failure.
With the gradual extension of materials under a steady tensile stress over a long period of high temperature conditions nearing the melting point of the material.
Suddenly when a material with no elasticity is put under excessive stress, or one with limited elasticity has no time to be elastic under excessive stress.

question: A large storage tank, located above ground, is being filled with petroleum (gasoline) . The tank eventually overflows and petroleum cascades to the ground. The subsequent vapor could spread and contact an ignition source located a considerable distance way. This initially results in a flashfire but is quickly follows by an explosion and series of fires engulfing the whole site. What is most likely to have prevented this incident?
options: Hazardous area classification and selection of suitable ignition-protected electrical and mechanical equipment.
A high-level alarm with an independent high level trip system and an automatic overprotection system.
Constant flow filling rate combined with accurate calculations of tank filling based manual level readings.
Local fire departments have sufficient training and resources to respond to induction fires and explosions.
